versions.body:
The north ferry dock at Northpoint will close for six weeks of scheduled maintenance, the harbor authority said Tuesday.

"This is routine work we do every few years," spokesperson Glen Morrow said. "Nothing about the dock is unsafe."

Ferries will dock at the temporary south landing. Expect a short walk and longer queues at rush hour.
versions.title: Northpoint dock closed for scheduled maintenance

versions.body:
The north ferry dock at Northpoint will close for six weeks of maintenance, the harbor authority said.

Update, Jan. 29: The harbor authority now says inspectors found a crack in one of the dock's support pylons during the work. The authority says the crack was found during maintenance and was not the reason for the closure.

"Nothing about the dock is unsafe," spokesperson Glen Morrow said when the closure was announced.

Ferries will dock at the temporary south landing. Expect a short walk and longer queues at rush hour.
versions.title: Northpoint dock closed for scheduled maintenance

versions.body:
Hundreds of dead fish washed up along a half-mile stretch of Calder Creek on Monday. State environmental officers took water samples near the Route 9 bridge.

Residents reported a sour smell and a grey film on the water. The state lab said an algae bloom after the warm September was "the most likely explanation" but would not rule anything out before results are in.

"We'd ask people to keep dogs out of the creek for now," officer Paula Brandt said.

Results are expected in four to six weeks.
versions.title: Fish die-off at Calder Creek under investigation

versions.body:
Hundreds of dead fish washed up along a half-mile stretch of Calder Creek on Oct. 13. State environmental officers took water samples near the Route 9 bridge.

Update, Dec. 9: The state lab says its results are "inconclusive". Oxygen levels were low, which fits an algae bloom, but two samples were damaged in transport and could not be tested. The lab does not plan to test again.

"We'd ask people to keep dogs out of the creek for now," officer Paula Brandt said in October.
versions.title: Fish die-off at Calder Creek under investigation

versions.title: Small fire at Kestrel warehouse, no injuries
versions.body:
Firefighters put out a small fire at a Kestrel Logistics warehouse on Dock Road early Monday. Nobody was hurt.

Fire Chief Ray Delgado said the fire started in an electrical panel in the loading area and was contained within twenty minutes. "There's nothing suspicious about it," Delgado said. "Old wiring, a cold night, a heater on the same circuit."

Kestrel said deliveries in Eastfield could be "a day or two" late this week.

corrections.text: An earlier version of this article said about 40,000 homes lost power and that an animal probably caused the fault. Calder Power now says about 14,000 homes were affected and that a transformer failed.

versions.body:
About 40,000 homes lost power on Tuesday evening after what the utility called "an animal-related fault" at the Harbor Street substation.

Traffic lights went dark across Eastfield and the 14 bus ran with flashlights. Power was back for most homes by 1 a.m.

"A squirrel, most likely," a Calder Power spokesperson said. "It happens more than you'd think."
versions.title: Blackout hits 40,000 homes across Port Calder
Blackout hits 14,000 homes across Port Calder
versions.body:
About 14,000 homes lost power on Tuesday evening after a fault at the Harbor Street substation.

Traffic lights went dark across Eastfield and the 14 bus ran with flashlights. Power was back for most homes by 1 a.m.

Calder Power first said an animal had probably caused the fault. On Thursday it said a transformer had failed and that no animal was involved.

versions.title: Calder Power: failed transformer, not an animal, caused blackout
versions.body:
Calder Power now says Tuesday's blackout was caused by a failed transformer at the Harbor Street substation. About 14,000 homes were affected, the company said, not 40,000 as it first estimated.

The company apologised for "early information that turned out to be wrong" and said the transformer was due to be replaced next year.

corrections.text: An earlier version said three crashes. City data shows four.

versions.title: Route 9 junction saw four crashes this year, city data shows
versions.body:
City data shows four crashes involving cyclists at the junction of Route 9 and Harbor Street so far this year, one of them fatal.

The council has delayed a protected bike lane at the junction twice. Councilmember Ana Ruiz said the lane is "a priority, but not the only priority".

Cycling groups plan a ride to City Hall in December.

versions.title: Kestrel driver rescues dog from icy harbor
versions.body:
A Kestrel Logistics driver jumped into the harbor at Pier 3 on Sunday to pull out a dog that had fallen through thin ice.

"I didn't think. You just go," said the driver, who asked not to be named. The dog, a beagle called Biscuit, is recovering.

Police arrested three men after a fight outside the Anchor bar on Harbor Street early Saturday, including the 24-year-old son of a city councilmember.

Two people were treated for minor injuries. All three men were released without charge on Sunday.

Port Calder High lockdown lifted after 'credible threat' turns out false
versions.body:
Port Calder High was locked down for two hours on Thursday after a phone call warning of an armed man near the school. Police found nobody. The call came from a number that no longer exists.

Principal Joan Ames thanked students "for staying calm and staying put".

comments.text: The 14 bus has now been diverted for longer than it has run.

Basement is fine. Car is not.

Water in the street, none in the tap. Classic Port Calder.

versions.title: Water main break floods Harbor Street
versions.body:
A water main burst under Harbor Street on Tuesday morning, flooding the road between 2nd and 5th and cutting water to about 600 homes.

Crews expect repairs to take "at least four days". Harbor Street is closed to traffic, and the 14 bus is diverted again.

The city said the pipe was "nearly a century old".

versions.title: Power restored after second outage in a month
versions.body:
Power is back in most of Eastfield after a second outage in less than a month. About 3,000 homes were affected for two hours on Saturday morning.

Calder Power said the new outage was "unrelated" to February's transformer failure.

versions.title: Harbor Street reopens after water main repair
versions.body:
Harbor Street reopened to traffic on Monday after six days of repairs. The 14 bus returns to its normal route on Tuesday.

The city said it will review all pipes older than 80 years "over the coming decade".

comments.text: Fixed the bus routes? Have you taken the 14?

versions.title: Mayor Harlan to seek third term
versions.body:
Mayor Denise Harlan will run for a third term, she told supporters at the Harbor Community Center on Monday night.

"We've fixed the bus routes, we've fixed the budget, and we're going to fix the harbor," Harlan said. No other candidate has declared.

versions.title: Council approves library hours cut
versions.body:
The city council voted 7–4 on Monday to close the Eastfield and Northpoint library branches on Mondays and Tuesdays from October, saving about $90,000 a year.

Librarians and parents spoke against the cut for two hours. "You are closing the only warm, free room in the neighborhood," one parent said.

versions.title: City budget leaves road repairs short again
versions.body:
The city's draft budget for 2026 sets aside $2.1 million for road repairs, about half of what the public works department says it needs.

"We are patching patches," public works director Hal Okonjo said.

versions.title: Kestrel Logistics adds 60 jobs at Dock Road
versions.body:
Kestrel Logistics will hire 60 drivers and warehouse staff at its Dock Road site this autumn, the company said. Most jobs are full-time.

Kestrel moved into the former Calder cannery building in 2023.

versions.title: Harbor Street shops say roadworks cost them a summer
versions.body:
Owners of six shops on Harbor Street say a summer of roadworks cut their takings by a third. "People just stopped coming down here," said Salty's Fish Bar owner Rosa Vitale.

The city says the work was "essential" and will be finished by spring.

versions.title: Calder Credit Union opens Eastfield branch
versions.body: Calder Credit Union opened its third branch on Monday, on 4th Street in Eastfield. The branch has two tellers and one very popular dish of free mints.

comments.text: End of an era. First date with my wife was at Salty's. 1979.

@harborgull Rosa deserves to retire without a conspiracy.
Chips night is on the calendar. Bringing all four.
Rent up, customers down. Same story all along Harbor Street.
The fryers are older than the building's current owners, whoever they are.
Who's going to sell me chowder in the fog now?

versions.title: Salty's Fish Bar to close after 55 years
versions.body:
Salty's Fish Bar, a Harbor Street fixture since 1971, will close at the end of April, owner Rosa Vitale said.

"The rent went up, the roadworks went on, and I'm tired," Vitale said. She would not say who bought the building.

Regulars are planning a farewell "chips night" on April 25.

versions.title: City launches app to report potholes
versions.body: Residents can now report potholes with a photo through the new CalderFix app. The city says it will respond to every report within ten working days. Early reviews say the app definately works better than the phone line, which nobody answered anyway.

versions.title: Bus tracker shows ghost buses, transit authority admits
versions.body: The live map on the transit authority's website has shown buses that do not exist, the authority admitted. 'It's a data feed problem,' a spokesperson said. Some riders say they waited half an hour for a 14 that was never there.

versions.title: Library adds e-reader lending
versions.body: Port Calder libraries now lend e-readers for three weeks at a time. Each comes loaded with 40 classics and a charger.

versions.title: Smart doorbells: what they record, and who sees it
versions.body: Smart doorbells now cover most front doors on some Eastfield streets. We asked three companies what happens to the footage. Two did not reply. One said it 'never shares data without a legal request', but would not say how many requests it gets.

versions.title: Is your phone listening? We tested it
versions.body: We spent a week talking about camping gear near a phone that had never searched for it. On day five, it showed us an ad for a tent. Our conclusion: probably not. But we definately bought a tent.

versions.title: Port Calder schools ban phones in class
versions.body: Phones will go in lockers during lessons at all three Port Calder high schools from January. Students can use them at lunch.

versions.title: Review: GlowNest lamp promises better sleep
versions.body: The GlowNest smart lamp dims slowly to orange in the evening and promises 'deeper, calmer sleep'. After two weeks, we slept the same, but the lamp is pretty.

versions.title: Smart meters: what the new boxes actually measure
versions.body: Calder Power has fitted smart meters in about a third of Eastfield homes since December. They report your use every half hour. They can also switch a home off remotely, the company confirmed, but it says it definately never has.

versions.title: Port Calder schools pilot AI homework helper
versions.body: Two middle schools will test an AI homework helper this spring. Teachers can see every question a student asks. 'It explains, it doesn't answer,' the district said. Parents can opt out.

versions.title: Harbor jazz nights return to the Anchor
versions.body: Jazz is back at the Anchor on Thursday nights from June, after a two-year break. The house band is the same four musicians, "slightly older and much louder," pianist Lou Benn said.

versions.title: Five walks for a foggy weekend
versions.body: Port Calder has fog the way other towns have weather. Our five favourite walks for when you can't see the end of your own arm: the harbor loop, the old rail path, Calder Creek trail, the lighthouse steps and the cemetery hill, which is quieter than it sounds.

versions.title: Rubber duck race returns to Harbor Festival
versions.body: The Harbor Festival's rubber duck race returns on Saturday, with 4,000 ducks and a new finish line at Pier 2. Proceeds go to the sea rescue service.

versions.title: Harbor Festival: the photos
versions.body:
Rain, chips and an estimated 9,000 people. Our photographer spent the day at the Harbor Festival. [Photo: the crowd at Pier 2]

The duck race was won by duck number 3,117, owned by eight-year-old Mila from Northpoint.

versions.title: The best chowder in Port Calder, ranked
versions.body: We ate eleven bowls of chowder in three days so you don't have to. Number one, still, is Salty's. Number eleven will not be named, out of kindness.

versions.title: Stop calling it 'the dead internet'
versions.body:
My nephew says nobody on the internet is real any more. "It's all bots, Uncle Marcus." I asked him how he knew. He said he read it online.

There are certainly more machines writing things than there used to be. But the conclusion that nobody is out there is a very lonely way to read a very noisy world. Write to me. I'll answer. Probably.

versions.title: Let the 14 bus be late in peace
versions.body: Every city has one bus that becomes a personality. Ours is the 14. It is late, it is diverted, and it is loved. I would not change a thing, except all of it.

versions.title: In praise of boring news
versions.body: This week we reported a water main, a power cut and a fish bar closing. Nobody was lied to and nobody went viral. I think that is what a local paper is for.

corrections.text: An earlier version misspelled Ms. Whitlock's name.

versions.title: Agnes Whitlock, 91, taught three generations to swim
versions.body:
Agnes Whitlock, who taught swimming at the Harbor pool for 44 years, died on April 26. She was 91.

"She would stand at the deep end with a whistle and a biscuit," her daughter said. "You got the biscuit at the end."

comments.text: He sold me my first duck. RIP Walter.

He always let the little ones hold the starting rope.
Good man. Terrible at darts.

versions.title: Walter Brennan, 81, harbor festival volunteer
versions.body:
Walter Brennan, who volunteered at every Harbor Festival since 1979, died on Oct. 31 after a short illness. He was 81.

Brennan ran the duck race for thirty years. "He knew half the ducks by name," a friend said.

corrections.text: An earlier version gave the bakery's address as Main Street. It is on Ferry Road.

versions.title: Ines Carvalho, 67, ran the Northpoint bakery
versions.body: Ines Carvalho, whose custard tarts drew queues down Northpoint's main street every Saturday, died on Jan. 8. She was 67. The bakery will stay open, her son said, "because she'd kill us if it didn't."

versions.title: Samuel Okoro, 74, lighthouse keeper
versions.body: Samuel Okoro, the last keeper of the Port Calder lighthouse before it was automated in 1998, died on Feb. 6. He was 74. He kept the logbook going for 27 years after there was nothing left to log.

versions.title: Harold Ng, 88, ferry captain
versions.body: Harold Ng, who captained the Eastfield–Northpoint ferry for 35 years and never once missed the 6:10, died on March 11. He was 88.

versions.title: Harbor Festival planning starts early this year
versions.body:
The Harbor Festival committee met for the first time on Tuesday, eight months before the festival.

"We want the duck race bigger than ever," said volunteer Walter Brennan, who has run the race for decades. "Five thousand ducks."

The committee is looking for volunteers to sort ducks in September.

versions.title: Same-day delivery comes to every Port Calder doorstep
versions.body: From today, Kestrel Logistics delivers same-day to every address in Port Calder. Order by noon, open your door by six. Kestrel: we know the way.

versions.title: Building Eastfield's next hundred years
versions.body: Port Calder was built by people who weren't afraid of the future. Northgate Development is proud to invest in Eastfield: new homes, new jobs and a waterfront everyone can enjoy.

versions.title: Sleep like the fog rolled in: meet GlowNest
versions.body: The GlowNest lamp learns when you wind down and dims with you. Thousands of five-star reviews. Free returns. Your best sleep is one lamp away.

corrections.text: An earlier version misspelled the advertiser's name as Harbour Dental.

versions.title: Smile, Port Calder: Harbour Dental now open late
versions.body: Harbor Dental now opens until 8 p.m. on weekdays. New patients get a free check-up and a toothbrush that is better than yours.

versions.title: Your neighbors bank here
versions.body: Calder Credit Union has served Port Calder since 1952. Now in Eastfield, on 4th Street. Free mints included.
